## Stock Return Prediction & Options Pricing

**Tools:** Python, pandas, scikit-learn, XGBoost, yfinance  
**Type:** Independent Machine Learning & Quantitative Finance Project

Developed an end-to-end machine learning pipeline to predict whether individual stocks would outperform the S&P 500 (SPY) over the following month.

Analyzed historical price data from 20 stocks across four sectors between 2018 and 2024.

### Methodology

- **Feature Engineering:** Created momentum, moving-average, and volatility indicators from historical stock prices.
- **Machine Learning:** Trained and evaluated Logistic Regression, Ridge Classifier, and XGBoost models using a chronological train-test split.
- **Backtesting:** Simulated a rolling stock-selection strategy that ranked stocks and selected the top five for an equally weighted portfolio.
- **Options Pricing:** Implemented Black-Scholes and Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial tree models to estimate theoretical European call option prices.

### Model Performance

| Model | Test Accuracy | AUC |
|---|---:|---:|
| Logistic Regression | 51.9% | 0.470 |
| Ridge Classifier | 52.5% | — |
| XGBoost | 50.0% | 0.493 |

The models performed near random classification accuracy, highlighting the difficulty of predicting short-term stock returns using historical price indicators alone.

### Historical Backtesting Results

| Metric | Strategy | S&P 500 (SPY) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total Return | 238.45% | 96.35% |
| Annualized Return | 32.49% | 16.85% |
| Sharpe Ratio | 1.275 | 1.035 |
| Maximum Drawdown | -17.73% | -23.93% |

*Backtest period: 2020–2024. These are exploratory results, not evidence of a reliable trading advantage. The analysis is subject to survivorship bias, a limited stock universe, and omitted transaction costs.*

### Key Takeaways

This project provided hands-on experience with financial data pipelines, feature engineering, machine learning model evaluation, rolling-window backtesting, and derivatives pricing.

It also reinforced the importance of evaluating predictive performance separately from simulated investment returns.


### Future Improvements

Currently exploring an expanded modeling approach using a larger S&P 500 stock universe, additional technical indicators, and comparisons between linear and nonlinear regression models.
